research_question: Can periodic algorithmic participation at quarter-hour openings create cross-market common-flow impulses whose confirmed followers offer frequent, independent and cost-positive passive continuation entries?

hypothesis.context: The first completed five-minute interval of each UTC quarter-hour is a recurring algorithmic liquidity and information-arrival window rather than an arbitrary optimized clock.
hypothesis.state: At least three of BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP must complete the same directional displacement with same-signed taker flow. The largest ATR-standardized body owns price discovery; only already-confirmed followers are tradable.
hypothesis.entry: Passive limit at the follower impulse midpoint, representing first consequent encroachment after a complete common-flow initiative.
hypothesis.invalidation: Beyond the follower impulse origin plus the inherited ATR buffer; reacceptance through the origin invalidates the new auction leg.
hypothesis.target: One complete follower impulse range projected from the impulse close, a measured-move delivery objective belonging to the same leg.
hypothesis.expiry: The next quarter-hour boundary. A plan that does not retrace before the next periodic information window is no longer the same episode.
hypothesis.independence: One causal event identity per quarter-hour window; simultaneous followers compete through the unchanged one-slot global arbitration. The information owner itself is never chased.

selection.method: Six already-exposed diagnostic weeks spanning 2021-2025. They can reject or redesign the scenario but cannot support a success claim.

claim_rules: E01-E06 are exposed development periods and cannot support a success claim.
No magnitude threshold or clock phase may be changed merely to recover trades from these periods.
A positive result must advance unchanged to a broader exposed screen, then a source freeze and untouched continuous validation.
